paper_title: Constraints on light decaying dark matter candidates from 16 years of INTEGRAL/SPI observations
notes: Paper presents new 95% CL exclusion limits on decaying dark matter from 16 years of INTEGRAL/SPI observations. Primary results are for two decay channels: monochromatic 2γ (60 keV–16 MeV) and FSR (1.1–200 MeV). For ALPs, the 2γ channel dominates and provides the strongest constraints. Data points extracted from Figure 3 (ALP-to-photon coupling g_agamma vs mass m_a) by visual inspection of the blue shaded exclusion region. The paper states these are 'the strongest constraints available in the literature' for ALP masses in the covered range. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.72) because: (1) coupling type is clear from context (AxionPhoton for ALPs), (2) numerical values are read from a figure rather than a table, introducing some uncertainty in precise values, (3) the paper clearly identifies this as a new measured limit at 95% CL. The FSR channel (Figure 4) constrains g_ae (AxionElectron) but with lower sensitivity due to α/(2π) suppression factor. Sterile neutrino bounds (Figure 5) are on sin²(2θ) mixing angle, not a standard coupling type. The analysis uses a Navarro-Frenk-White DM profile but this is a galactic morphology template, not a local DM density assumption for a haloscope experiment, so dm_density_assumed is null. | selector: text (sole candidate)
